To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
testosterone increases cAMP levels and cAMP-dependent protein kinase activity in cultured bovine aortic endothelial cells, and estradiol has a stimulatory effect on cAMP metabolism in these cells.

The effects of testosterone and 17β-estradiol on the cyclic nucleotide metabolisms in primary cultured bovine endothelial cells are different from those of the corresponding sex steroids in the intact animal.

the addition of testosterone to the culture medium of bovine endothelial cells increased the intracellular levels of cAMP, cGMP and cAMP-dependent protein kinase activity, and that the addition of estradiol increased the intracellular cAMP level and the activity of the cAMP-dependent protein kinases, while the cGMP level and the cGMP-dependent protein kinase activity were not affected.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of sex hormones on the cyclic nucleotide metabolisms in cultured bovine aortic endothelial cells.
the effects of testosterone on endothelial cell function.
the effect of sex hormones on cyclic nucleotide metabolism and the role of cyclic nucleotides in the action of sex hormones.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
sex steroids have a significant impact on the function of the cardiovascular system and on the pathophysiological processes leading to cardiovascular disease.
the effects of estradiol on endothelial function are complex and depend on the dose and the duration of exposure, the vascular bed, and the species.
the effects of estradiol and testosterone on the cardiovascular system are mediated by a complex network of mechanisms that involve the endothelial cells and vascular smooth muscle cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
testosterone is a powerful regulator of endothelial cell function, which may be mediated in part by the modulation of cAMP and cGMP metabolism.
we have demonstrated that the sex hormones estradiol and testosterone regulate the expression of endothelial nitric oxide synthase (eNOS) in cultured endothelial cells.
we have shown that the effects of sex hormones on the cyclic nucleotide system of bovine aortic endothelial cells are complex.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the endothelium is a very dynamic organ that is able to sense and respond to the environment, and that it is not just a passive barrier.
we have shown that the effects of testosterone are not limited to the vascular system.
the sex hormone estrogen can protect the brain from damage caused by a stroke, and that this protective effect may be mediated by a mechanism that is not yet fully understood.
